Not just in terms of population, but technology, globalization, and pretty much everything.
What are your opinions on Humanity's exponential growth?

Personally, I don't think we as a species were ever supposed to be this advanced or have a population this large. That's not to say it's a bad thing (though, I think in same ways it is), but it just gets ya thinkin'. Y'know?
Why do you feel we should never have reached this level of advancement? And when you say "advanced", do you mean technologically, evolutionarily or what?

Mostly technologically. We have the ability to expand our life by decades, and that's advancing even more by the day. We have the ability to traverse the world within mere hours. We can contact people on the other side of the world within seconds. But at the same time we're taking more than the Earth can provide. Ecologically speaking, we shouldn't have made it this far. And as a species we're bar none. With the advent of modern weaponry we're fucking invincible (except against ourselves, obviously). And with domesticated animals and agriculture we don't even have to risk going far to get the essential things.

I don't think we've come 'too far' with a lot of these things.

Life expectancy really isn't advancing at this point - it has plateaued and we will need more major breakthroughs before we see a continued rise. The main reason mean life expectancy was considerably lower in times past was higher infant mortality; those who survived childhood had a considerably higher life expectancy than the average. While technological advances were responsible for this, many of those lives were saved by innovations as simple as sanitation and antibiotics.

As for agriculture, we've been cultivating plants for 23,000 years, we domesticated dogs 35,000 years ago, and have been domesticating lifestock for the last 12,000 years. You might as well say that our discovery/control of fire is too technologically advanced.

"Supposed" implies that there was a purpose for us before we were created. There was no intention. We just are. If we weren't, then another organism would be.

It is more accurate to say that we aren't equipped to be this advanced or have a population this large.

No one species has had such a lock down on the planet, has it? My worry is what if we get to the top of that curve? Will our technology be able to support our exponential growth of population? Because that is the reason we are thriving right now. My opinion on it, is that it is unnatural, but at the same time, we are the ones benefiting from it, so it is hard to look outside that.

Population growth slows down. It isn't exponential. Look at Japan. Either way humanity will always solve its problems. Its just too many potential geniuses are stuck in third world countries never knowing they were.

We were never supposed to grow this big and nature will regulate things eventually. (thats if we dont go first and fuck the planet up)

2 billion people is the most Earth can hold without running out of recourses.

If there is a war and some survive, birthrates must be caped for the future.

We were never supposed to grow this big and nature will regulate things eventually.

Yep, it's already starting...

2 billion people is the most Earth can hold without running out of recourses

2 billion people living which kind of lifestyle ? American, European, Indian, African ? Resource depletion depends not only on demography but also heavily on our way of life, for example Americans represent 5% of the world population but use over 20% of Earth's resources. We would need four planets if everybody was to live like an American.

Unless we keep having revolutions (like the Industrial Revolution, Technological Revolution, etc.) we won't be able to continue the exponential growth we've had in these areas since around 1800. I'm cautiously optimistic that so long as we don't destroy ourselves we'll probably stabilise at a certain point when Earth is about as full as it can ecologically sustain. If we get to point of colonising other planets, we'll probably start growing again until we begin to reach that capacity.

Technology cannot continue to grow at this pace indefinitely. There is a finite limit to the laws that govern reality, consequently a finite time over which science is productive. When scientific discovery slows, technological innovation will also. This likely won't be in our lifetimes, but it will occur if we don't wipe out civilization.

As for human population, the planet may be able to support more, but with our current progress in technology and politics, it is struggling to sustain those it has - especially in areas like the third world. We need to take drastic action to slow growth, thereby giving technology a chance to catch up. We should be focused on quality of life for the population that exists, not expansion.

I remember reading something about the human population stabilizing around 10 or 11 billion people. As society becomes more advanced birthrates have fallen in developed countries; some first world countries would actually be declining in population without immigrants.

It's absolutely the case that birth rates have dropped in first world countries. From what I understand, with increased education, women become more focused on their careers and put off having children, consequently have fewer. The concern really is countries outside the first world. If you look at what is happening in Europe at present, there are countless economic refugees (immigrants) who are leaving Africa and the Middle East in the hope of a better life. It is to the point where members of their parliaments have discussed deploying naval assets to forcefully repel the boats. There is a similar situation in the US, and there was a similar situation in Australia until recently.

Many of these third world countries are no longer self-sufficient and rely heavily on foreign aid. As their populations continue to soar, that aid will get stretched thin and eventually be insufficient. What we see at the moment in Europe is just the first wave - those who are choosing to get out before things become worse. When the time comes, though, we will see literally millions of refugees storming borders - desperate to survive at any cost. If we don't address this issue before it happens, I am doubtful that the first world nations will prevail, other than through all out war. It would be better if we acted now to help the third world nations take control of their crises, and prevent this escalation.

I guess I'm more of a pessimist on the topic than you guys. I think we are dooming our species by continuing to grow. I can't see any way that it's healthy for us or our planet. I also don't see any way to stop it. You'll never convince enough people that they should be the ones to sacrifice having children and a family to remotely make a difference. I often daydream of what it would be like if there were only 100k people on the planet. Or even just a million. Nature seems to have a way of correcting though. We'd be fools to think we're above that. Disease, famine, global disaster. We try to help the cause by killing each other but it's still not enough. Like I said...maybe I'm the pessimist...I'm sure it'll all work out...

I think populations will stabilize after a while. Too much people -> more death.

Nature always finds a way.

We should actively work to reduce it. Now I'm not saying that we should run around killing people but there are ways to reduce the population. We could invest in raising the standard of living in the countries with the highest birth rates (Birth rate negatively correlates with standard of living). We could also give people proper sex education (not abstinence only, that's BS) and easy access to birth control and condoms to reduce the number of unplanned/ unwanted pregnancies.

Overpopulation is not the problem, because everyone could fit in Texas.

Feeding the world is not the problem, because we already produce enough food for everyone.

Many people seem to be worried about these, but I think that the real problem with the growing population is getting what people need to the people who need it. The real problem is transportation.
